subject: Technical follow-up: latency, throughput & streaming checkpoints for hosted PoC
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Technical follow-up: latency, throughput & streaming checkpoints for hosted PoC

Emma — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the technical checkpoints we agreed would help us size the hosted PoC and validate p95/p99 targets end-to-end. I captured the items below so we can align the PoC scope and the data we need from your side.

High-level acceptance targets (your ask):
- p95 end-to-end (client edge -> app -> Redwood hosted API -> client): goal <= 250 ms
- p99 end-to-end: goal <= 700 ms
- Sustained throughput: ~60 req/s across the fleet (steady-state)
- Burst concurrency: spikes up to 350 concurrent in short windows (1–5 min)
- Typical request size: ~120 response tokens / ~200 input tokens (approx)
- Streaming: yes — token-level partial responses (SSE) with early-flush for first token within 50–100 ms after generation begins

What we need from Acme before we spin up PoC:
1) Traffic profile (CSV or sample logs) with per-minute counts for at least a 48-hour window and a 1-week aggregate — include request size distribution and % streaming vs batch.
2) Example request payloads (3–5 typical prompts) and any post-processing done client-side.
3) Current provider baselines: p95/p99 numbers (end-to-end if possible), per-region, and any edge caching or CDN behavior you observe.
4) IP allowlist / egress constraints for the PoC endpoints and preferred region (us-west1 or us-east4).
5) Success criteria: please confirm whether matching incumbent p99 is an absolute requirement or if a bounded delta (e.g., <= +150 ms) is acceptable during the PoC.

Next steps / timeline proposal:
- You: share traffic_profile.csv and sample payloads by EOD Thu 8/12
- Redwood: provide PoC test plan (+ prelim infra estimate) within 48 hours of receiving data
- Align on start date & synthetic traffic windows to mirror production mix

Attachments: we’ll expect your traffic_profile file (please send as CSV). I attached a short checklist (poc-test-plan.pdf) to show the typical test steps we run.

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Irene in since they’ll run the PoC and triage any tuning.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@acmehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: platform+acme@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical follow-up: latency, throughput & streaming checkpoints for hosted PoC

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the clear checklist. Attaching the traffic profile we discussed (acme_traffic_profile_v2.csv). A few clarifications from our side:

- Our production end-to-end numbers (vendor -> app -> client) measure roughly p95=120 ms, p99=420 ms in our primary region (us-west). Note: the incumbent uses an edge cache for a subset of requests which skews p95 down for cached paths.
- Average sustained throughput for the last 30 days: ~42 req/s. Peak bursts during marketing events hit ~380 concurrent for ~3–6 minutes.
- Typical request characteristics: median input ~140 tokens, median output ~110 tokens. Our clients rely on streaming to show partial results — losing token-level updates would be a UX regression.
- For the PoC we can provide logs (sanitized) and sample payloads; however, we cannot provide full raw PII logs. We will sanitize and provide request timing windows.

Questions from Acme:
1) If Redwood’s hosted API needs to route to multiple models (small vs large) for cost/latency tradeoffs, can you guarantee consistent streaming semantics and order of tokens across variants?
2) Are there any additional headers or connection settings we must set to ensure low-latency streaming (keep-alive, chunked encoding, SSE expected)?

We can deliver the CSV and sample prompts by end of day Thu 8/12 as requested.

— Emma
Emma Thomas | Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Health
emma.thomas@acmehealth.com | +1 617-555-8899
Attachment: acme_traffic_profile_v2.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@acmehealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical follow-up: latency, throughput & streaming checkpoints for hosted PoC

Emma — great context, thanks for the CSV. A few responses and a proposed PoC scoping note: 

1) Streaming semantics across model variants: we guarantee FIFO token ordering and identical streaming behavior (chunking/flush cadence) across model families supported in the PoC. If you choose a lighter model for cheaper token costs, streaming cadence is preserved; absolute latency per token may vary but ordering and partial-flush semantics are consistent.

2) Connection settings: we recommend HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive and a client-side socket timeout >= 60s. For server-sent events (SSE) or chunked transfer, ensure your client accepts partial responses and does not buffer at the HTTP library level. We’ll share a short checklist of headers and examples in the test plan.

Proposed PoC scope (2 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): exchange IP allowlist, deliver sanitized traffic CSV, and sign PoC MSA
- Week 1: mirror production steady-state traffic at 1x and run token-level streaming validation (functional correctness + time-to-first-token)
- Week 2: synthetic burst windows to validate p95/p99 under concurrency spikes and autoscaling behavior; run fallback scenarios to smaller variants if we detect degradation

Success criteria (suggested):
- p95 within +100 ms of incumbent for non-cached paths, p99 within +200 ms, and no regression in streaming token ordering or partial flush behavior
- No loss of tokens or reordering observed in >99.9% of streaming sessions during tests

We can attach a formal PoC test plan and a short MSA for PoC work (DocuSign link below). If that looks good, the legal/ops folks can execute quickly and we’ll schedule the prep session.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/poC-MSA-ACME
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-678901

Attachment: poc-test-plan.pdf

— Ben
